why: train.py line citations still carrying a bare number, in both forms the check reads: the qualified `train.py:NNN` and the abbreviated `:NNN` inside a sentence that names train.py and no sha. A RATCHET -- a NEW bare citation FAILs check_train_cite_targets. Ruling (aupai-4c, 2026-09-06 and the abbreviated-form narrowing 2026-09-07): cite a role or a symbol, or anchor the number to a commit sha. Every entry is DEBT, not an exception: the 2026-09-06 audit read the 198 qualified citations under scripts/ and 103 of 118 judgement cases were rotten, so assume these are mostly rotten too and read each one before believing it. 4c has ordered the audit of these, eval/ first, one commit per directory, shrinking this list each time.
schema: allowed_bare maps `<citing file>-><cited number>` to HOW MANY bare citations that pair may carry. CONTENT-KEYED, NOT POSITION-KEYED, and a MULTISET rather than a set. The first schema keyed on `<file>:<citing line>-><target>` and any insertion above a baselined citation moved its key, turning the ratchet red on whoever merged next (4c, 2026-09-07; e1 hit it landing #48, 122 lines inserted, key 6174 -> 6285). A line-text hash was the other candidate and trades one false red for another: measured, it gives 87 distinct keys for 87 citations against this key's 70, but it goes red on a comment REFLOW, which happens whenever a sentence around a citation is edited. The count is what keeps the ratchet honest under a colliding key: 15 pairs carry more than one citation, so a set would let a file grow from one to three with the baseline unchanged.
count_growth_reason: 2 BARE of 34 TARGETS, 32 sha-anchored and verified at their sha. THE DENOMINATOR CHANGED 2026-09-08 and every count this file carried before then was over CITATIONS where a reader takes it over TARGETS: _CITE_RE was `train.py:(\d+)`, which matches the FIRST number in a comma list and stops, so eff.kda_kernel_path's five-number list was ONE target and only :93 was ever resolved. Tree-wide that hid 11 unresolved targets behind a PASS reading `21 citation(s): 19 sha-anchored and verified` -- 3 comma lists and 3 ranges. A range names its ENDPOINTS, not every line between -- 454-537 spans 84 lines and any well-formed function body has blank lines inside it. This ratchet was part of the same defect and is fixed with it: it did `int(m.group(1))`, which crashed on '701-706' the moment the regex widened, and it now calls the gate's own _cite_line_numbers so the two cannot disagree. THE SWEEP ITSELF IS CLOSED at 125 -> 2: both survivors are quoted TORCH_LOGS=recompiles output ('Recompiling function forward in /work/aupai/train.py:521' and the muon_update one at :746), which cannot become symbols without falsifying a quotation. 74 of 74 citations judged across the six facts/ files were rotten; code side zero since 2026-09-07 morning. THE THREE CLASSES, because a future sweep meets them again: (1) the ordinary case, 14 entries that already named the symbol beside the number, where the number was redundant; (2) quoted tool output, kept verbatim; (3) a citation describing a defect SINCE FIXED -- eff.run_end_cursor_overstates_under_max_steps, whose five numbers describe the run-end save before c9011022 gave it opt and step, so a symbol would aim a reader at code that now does the opposite; a content search over every train.py commit 2026-08-28..2026-09-05 found no sha holding all five at their lines, so it carries 'lines as recorded'. A fourth was found and dropped rather than classified: eff.kda_kernel_path cited :211, which is `q,` -- a bare argument that resolves and is non-blank, so the gate passes it forever while it carries no content any reader could check the claim against. An anchor in form, not in substance. Two more were JSON KEYS rather than prose and took a sha anchor from their entry's own the_one_commit, 169da865. A new bare citation anywhere FAILs.
